name: SmartTensors
summary: Framework for unsupervised, supervised, and physics-informed machine learning with matrix/tensor factorization methods.
description: SmartTensors is a framework for science-informed ML/AI using methods such as NMFk and NTFk for feature extraction, model diagnostics, and robust analyses of complex datasets.
details: SmartTensors is a general framework for unsupervised, supervised, and physics-informed machine learning using nonnegative matrix and tensor decomposition algorithms.
The framework includes NMFk and NTFk methods for extracting hidden features, spatial footprints, and temporal signatures from complex datasets with minimal prior assumptions.
SmartTensors algorithms are written in Julia and can be integrated with Flux.jl, TensorFlow, PyTorch, MXNet, and MATLAB.
SmartTensors has been supported for commercial deployment through the DOE Technology Commercialization Fund.
highlights: NMFk and NTFk for nonnegative matrix and tensor factorization
Feature extraction, anomaly detection, image recognition, and model diagnostics
Designed for science-informed AI and reduced-order modeling workflows

name: MADS
summary: Model Analysis and Decision Support framework for calibration, uncertainty quantification, and diagnostics.
description: MADS is an open-source high-performance framework for model inversion, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, and decision support across environmental and geoscience applications.
details: MADS, or Model Analysis and Decision Support, is an integrated open-source high-performance computational framework for data and model analysis.
It has been tested on multi-processor clusters and cloud environments and provides adaptive workflows that reduce manual setup for complex analyses.
MADS can couple to external simulators through template and instruction files and also includes built-in analytical groundwater and contaminant-transport simulators.
The framework has been used for environmental site characterization, source identification, uncertainty quantification, model calibration, and monitoring optimization.
highlights: Sensitivity analysis, parameter estimation, inversion, and calibration
Uncertainty quantification, model selection, and surrogate modeling
Machine learning, blind source separation, and decision analysis

name: WELLS
summary: Analytical simulator for multi-well pumping drawdown analysis in confined, unconfined, and leaky aquifers.
description: WELLS simulates pumping and injection well effects using analytical solutions and superposition to support aquifer test interpretation and groundwater decision support.
details: WELLS simulates drawdowns caused by multiple pumping or injecting wells using analytical solutions in both C and Julia implementations.
It can represent confined, unconfined, and leaky aquifers and uses superposition to account for transient pumping schedules and multiple well sources.
WELLS can also account for non-pumping water-level trends and early-time behavior using exponential functions for transmissivity and storativity effects.
Model inversion of WELLS predictions can be performed with MADS for calibration and uncertainty analysis.
highlights: Confined, unconfined, and leaky aquifer solutions
Fully and partially penetrating pumping and observation wells
Transient pumping rates with step-change and linear-change options

name: RegAE.jl
summary: Regularized inverse analysis using variational autoencoders for high-dimensional parameter fields.
description: RegAE.jl provides a VAE-based approach for regularizing inverse problems and reducing parameter-space complexity while preserving coherent structures.
details: RegAE.jl provides an efficient way to regularize inverse problems where parameter fields are high-dimensional and exhibit coherent structures.
The approach leverages a variational autoencoder to learn useful regularization behavior from unconditioned realizations without requiring prior knowledge of the governing physics.
By easing the regularization process and reducing the dimensionality of the optimized parameter space, RegAE.jl can make inverse analyses more computationally tractable.
Adjoint methods and automatic differentiation can be used to further reduce computational cost during inverse analysis workflows.
highlights: Supports lower-cost optimization through dimensionality reduction

name: PhysicsInformedML.jl
summary: Physics-informed machine learning subroutines for integrating scientific constraints into ML workflows.
description: PhysicsInformedML.jl contains reusable subroutines for incorporating physical constraints into learning pipelines and model diagnostics.
details: PhysicsInformedML.jl packages reusable subroutines for bringing scientific and physical constraints into machine learning workflows.
It complements broader SmartTensors-style workflows by helping combine data-driven learning with domain knowledge and model diagnostics.
The package is designed for Julia-based scientific ML pipelines where interpretability and physical consistency matter.
highlights: Supports science-informed diagnostics and workflow integration
Designed for Julia scientific machine learning pipelines

name: SVR.jl
summary: Support Vector Regression tools for data-driven regression analysis.
description: SVR.jl provides support vector regression utilities used in model analysis and data-driven prediction workflows.
details: SVR.jl provides support vector regression capabilities for data-driven regression analysis and predictive modeling workflows.
It fits naturally within the broader MADS and scientific data analytics ecosystem for surrogate modeling and structured regression tasks.
The package offers a lightweight Julia-based option for teams needing interpretable regression utilities alongside other analytical workflows.
highlights: Support vector regression for predictive modeling
Useful for surrogate modeling and data-driven analysis
Lightweight Julia package for regression workflows
